audit_findings.title: Completed Breeze acquisition is absent from the earnings numerator
audit_findings.mechanism: The anchor OE excludes Breeze's post-close earnings and acquisition financing costs even though the shares and balance-sheet context are post-close.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company intends to fund the Breeze Autocare acquisition with a newly issued $ 740 million Term Loan B commensurate with the closing of the transaction with excess proceeds being used to pay down outstanding debt.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated perimeter mismatch. Breeze closed on December 1, 2025, added 159 retained stores after the required 45-store divestiture, represented 8% of nine-month revenue and 20% of consolidated assets, and contributed filed post-close revenue of $117.1 million and net income of $13.1 million through June 2026. Recurring interest expense increased $22.8 million year over year, largely from the Term Loan B. These figures do not establish normalized incremental OE, so the direction remains unknown, but the acquisition is reasonably capable of changing the valuation materially.
audit_findings.action: Rebuild OE from post-close consolidated results, separating Breeze operating cash generation, the $57.9 million divestiture loss, $16.7 million of transaction costs, integration costs, acquired-intangible amortization, finance leases and all Term Loan B interest; rerun all scenarios without separately deducting ordinary debt principal.

audit_findings.title: Growth is credited without a visible charge for the capital that produces it
audit_findings.magnitude: computed first-year reinvestment of approximately $26.7 million in BASE and $55.0 million in BULL
audit_findings.mechanism: Positive growth increases forecast OE and terminal value, but the disclosed method does not show a corresponding reinvestment deduction from distributable cash flow.
audit_findings.evidence: Free cash flow excluding growth capital expenditures provides a supplemental view of cash flow generation before investments in growth capital, which expand future business operations, including the opening or expansion of retail service center stores and service capabilities.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated omission in the disclosed valuation mechanics: RONTA is displayed, but no reinvestment charge is identified. Using the supplied 26.4% RONTA, next-year OE multiplied by growth divided by RONTA implies approximately $26.7 million of first-year reinvestment for 3% growth and $55.0 million for 6% growth. Because terminal value is about half of operating PV, capital-free growth can materially overstate both explicit-period cash flows and terminal value.
audit_findings.action: Rerun BASE and BULL with an explicit annual reinvestment deduction equal to the capital required by each year's growth and the 26.4% RONTA, including during the fade to 2.5%, and reconcile that deduction to reported growth capital expenditures.

audit_findings.title: Finance-lease asset consumption may disappear from owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $36.4 million of FY2025 finance-lease assets obtained, equal to 15.9% of the $228.3 million anchor; valuation effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Adding back depreciation while deducting only cash capital expenditures can omit the replacement cost of assets financed through leases because lease principal is classified as financing cash flow.
audit_findings.evidence: Non-cash transactions, including finance leases, recognized within total property, plant and equipment were $ 64.2 million and $ 18.3 million during the years ended September 30, 2025 and 2024, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing establishes substantial finance-lease additions, but the supplied OE build does not show whether an economic replacement charge was retained. The $36.4 million of FY2025 finance-lease assets obtained is large relative to the anchor, although some additions may be growth assets rather than maintenance. The record therefore cannot establish the recurring omitted amount or its valuation materiality.
audit_findings.action: Trace finance-lease depreciation, additions, principal payments and interest through the FY2025 OE calculation; classify additions between maintenance and growth and rerun with the recurring maintenance component deducted once, without double counting interest.

audit_findings.title: Underfunded benefit plans are an unbridged senior claim
audit_findings.magnitude: $151.7 million, or $1.18 per diluted share and 4.6% of BASE equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Any normalized funding shortfall not already borne in OE should reduce the equity bridge or be reflected through future cash contributions.
audit_findings.evidence: Pension and other postretirement plans were underfunded by $151.7 million at September 30, 2025 as the projected benefit obligation exceeded the fair value of plan assets.
audit_findings.explanation: The bridge omission is demonstrated, although deducting the entire funded-status deficit immediately would be conservative because filed OE may already bear some contributions. Even that full deduction would reduce BASE value from $25.58 to about $24.40 per share and BULL value from $30.06 to about $28.88, leaving every scenario below the $32.03 market price and far above neither the 30% margin-of-safety threshold nor the existing no-buy conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Confirm whether normalized OE includes expected non-qualified payments and qualified-plan contributions; if not, add a probability-weighted contribution schedule or deduct the unrecognized claim in the bridge.

audit_findings.title: Transaction-specific costs may be embedded permanently in the anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: $15.8 million pretax; computed upper-bound BASE effect approximately $163 million or $1.27 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: A transaction-specific expense embedded in FY2025 OE is capitalized through the anchor as though it recurs, lowering forecast OE and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: Additionally, investment and divestiture activity increased SG&A expenses by $15.8 million, primarily related to consulting fees and professional services to support legal, regulatory, diligence and integration efforts.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing quantifies $15.8 million of investment and divestiture-related SG&A but does not establish how much was paid in FY2025 or is genuinely nonrecurring. As an upper-bound sensitivity, treating all $15.8 million as nonrecurring, tax-effecting it at 26.5%, and applying the reported BASE PV-to-anchor multiple adds about $1.27 per share. BASE would remain around $26.85 and the buy-below level around $18.80, both below the $32.03 price; a comparable BULL sensitivity remains approximately $31.56. Thus it can refine value but does not change the conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $15.8 million to cash paid and the anchor, separate one-time Breeze diligence and legal costs from recurring acquisition and integration costs, and normalize only the documented nonrecurring after-tax amount.

audit_findings.title: Unrecorded lease guarantees create contingent claims ahead of equity
audit_findings.magnitude: $93.4 million latest filed maximum exposure, or $0.73 per diluted share and 2.8% of BASE equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Defaults by buyers of divested businesses could create cash payments not included in historical OE or the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: The undiscounted maximum potential future payments under the lease guarantees were $63.8 million as of September 30, 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a contingent rather than demonstrated loss. The latest 10-Q increased the undiscounted maximum lease-guarantee exposure from $63.8 million to $93.4 million, but no liability was recorded because payment was not considered probable and no default is supplied. Even the undiscounted maximum equals only 2.8% of BASE equity value; expected loss should be materially lower absent deterioration. It should therefore be monitored rather than charged presently.
audit_findings.action: Monitor buyer and franchisee credit quality, guarantee expirations, post-close amendments and defaults each quarter; probability-weight expected payments and rerun the bridge if defaults occur or payment becomes reasonably possible.
